title: Rama protects Vishvamitra's ritual
introduction: Sage Vishwamitra travels to Mithila kingdom to attend a ritual of King Janaka and also to see the auspicious bow of Shiva that is being worshipped in the palace of Janaka from ages. The other sages suggest to Rama, that he too may go over there along with them to see that marvellous bow. They all proceed from Siddha Ashram towards River SoNa, a tributary of Ganga, and camp on its bank for a night.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये बाल काण्डे एक त्रिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 31st chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
अथ ताम् रजनीम् तत्र कृतार्थौ राम लक्षणौ |
ऊषतुर् मुदितौ वीरौ प्रहृष्टेन अंतरात्मना
verses.iast:
atha tām rajanīm tatra kṛtārthau rāma lakṣaṇau |
ūṣatur muditau vīrau prahṛṣṭena antarātmanā
verses.translation: Rejoicing for achieving the result of their journey with Vishvamitra, the brave Rama and Lakshmana then resided in that hermitage for that night, gladdening in their heart of hearts.

glosses.meaning: well, gladdened, in inner, souls - heart of hearts

verses.devanagari:
प्रभातायाम् तु शर्वर्याम् कृत पौर्व अह्णिक क्रियौ |
विश्वामित्रम् ऋषीम् च अन्यान् सहितौ अभिजग्मतुः
verses.iast:
prabhātāyām tu śarvaryām kṛta paurva ahṇika kriyau |
viśvāmitram ṛṣīm ca anyān sahitau abhijagmatuḥ
verses.translation: When that night turned into a new day, performing their morning chores both of the brother jointly approached Sage Vishvamitra, who is along with other sages by then.

glosses.meaning: to Vishvamitra, to other, sages, also

verses.devanagari:
अभिवाद्य मुनि श्रेष्ठम् ज्वलंतम् इव पावकम् |
ऊचतुर् परमोदारम् वाक्यम् मधुर भाषिणौ
verses.iast:
abhivādya muni śreṣṭham jvalantam iva pāvakam |
ūcatur paramodāram vākyam madhura bhāṣiṇau
verses.translation: And those gentle-speakers on reverencing that eminent sage Vishvamitra, whose radiance is akin to the ritual-fire, they two spoke this highly courteous sentence to him.

glosses.meaning: gentle, two speakers - Rama and Lakshmana

verses.devanagari:
इमौ स्म मुनि शार्दूल किंकरौ समुपस्थितौ |
आज्ञापय मुनिश्रेष्ठ शासनम् करवाव किम्
verses.iast:
imau sma muni śārdūla kiṅkarau samupasthitau |
ājñāpaya muniśreṣṭha śāsanam karavāva kim
verses.translation: "Oh, tigerly-sage, here are your attendants sir, available in your attendance, what order is to be carried out further, oh, eminent saint, that you may order us.

glosses.meaning: what, orders, we have to carry out.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्ते तयोः वाक्यम् सर्व एव महर्षयः |
विश्वामित्रम् पुरस्कृत्य रामम् वचनम् अब्रुवन्
verses.iast:
evam uk{}te tayoḥ vākyam sarva eva maharṣayaḥ |
viśvāmitram puraskṛtya rāmam vacanam abruvan
verses.translation: When they have said that way all those great sages spoke to Rama, keeping Vishvamitra at the helm of affairs.

glosses.meaning: by them, sentence, that way, when said
Vishvamitra, keeping ahead - at helm of affairs

verses.devanagari:
मैथिलस्य नरश्रेष्ठ जनकस्य भविष्यति |
यज्नः परम धर्मिष्ठः तत्र यास्यामहे वयम्
verses.iast:
maithilasya naraśreṣṭha janakasya bhaviṣyati |
yajnaḥ parama dharmiṣṭhaḥ tatra yāsyāmahe vayam
verses.translation: "Oh, best one among men, a highly righteous Vedic ritual belonging to King Janaka of Mithila is going to take place, and we the sages are going over there.

verses.devanagari:
त्वम् चैव नरशार्दूल सह अस्माभिर् गमिष्यसि |
अद्भुतम् च धनू रत्नम् तत्र त्वम् द्रष्टुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
tvam caiva naraśārdūla saha asmābhir gamiṣyasi |
adbhutam ca dhanū ratnam tatra tvam draṣṭum arhasi
verses.translation: "Oh, tigerly-man Rama, if you can come along with us, it will be expedient for you to see a monumental gem of bow there.
notes: The sages are not insisting on Rama to come along, but advising him to have a glimpse of that marvellous bow of Shiva, which none can lift to string, so far. The topic of Seetha is also not brought out by them, either, because it is in the know of Vishvamitra alone, and not known to these sages. Kings and princes have their own protocol of proper invitation. Here a third party is inviting Rama to some other king's ritual, which Rama may reject for being a prince. But it is suggestive to say the maxim an āhūto adhvaryam gacchet 'even uninvited can attend a Vedic-ritual...' Thus the sages are tempting, rather than inviting Rama to come to Mithila in the name of a divine bow, seeing which any valiant prince would easily get excited to string.

glosses.meaning: if you go - if you come with us
you, to see, expedient for you.

verses.devanagari:
तद्धि पूर्वम् नरश्रेष्ठ दत्तम् सदसि दैवतैः |
अप्रमेय बलम् घोरम् मखे परम भास्वरम्
verses.iast:
taddhi pūrvam naraśreṣṭha dattam sadasi daivataiḥ |
aprameya balam ghoram makhe parama bhāsvaram
verses.translation: "Oh, best one among men, in early times indeed gods gave that awesome bow which has an unimaginable power and which is superbly incandescent in wars to an erstwhile king of Mithila in a congregation of a Vedic-ritual.
notes: This is the bow of Shiva with which He destroyed the ritual of Daksha. Then gods pleased Shiva and obtained this bow from Him. Then gods gave it to Devaraata, an earlier king of Mithila as a boon of Vedic-ritual.

glosses.meaning: in Vedic-ritual congregation, given [to an erstwhile king,] indeed.

verses.devanagari:
न अस्य देवा न गंधर्वा न असुरा न च राक्षसाः |
कर्तुम् आरोपणम् शक्ता न कथंचन मानुषाः
verses.iast:
na asya devā na gandharvā na asurā na ca rākṣasāḥ |
kartum āropaṇam śak{}tā na kathañcana mānuṣāḥ
verses.translation: "Gods cannot capably lift it to string; gandharva-s, no; asura-s, no; demons, no; and for human beings, not in any way.

glosses.meaning: lifting for stinging, to make - to lift

verses.devanagari:
धनुषस्य तस्य वीर्यम् हि जिज्ञासन्तो महीक्षितः |
न शेकुर् आरोपयितुम् राजपुत्रा महाबलाः
verses.iast:
dhanuṣasya tasya vīryam hi jijñāsanto mahīkṣitaḥ |
na śekur āropayitum rājaputrā mahābalāḥ
verses.translation: "Though many kings were inquisitive about the power of that bow, all of those great mighty princes are rendered incapable to string its bowstring.

verses.devanagari:
तद् धनुर् नरशार्दूल मैथिलस्य महात्मनः |
तत्र द्रक्ष्यसि काकुत्स्थ यज्ञम् च परम अद्भुतम्
verses.iast:
tad dhanur naraśārdūla maithilasya mahātmanaḥ |
tatra drakṣyasi kākutstha yajñam ca parama adbhutam
verses.translation: "Oh, tigerly-man Rama, there in Mithila you can see that particular bow of the great-souled king of Mithila and his highly admirable Vedic ritual too, if you come with us.

glosses.meaning: there, you can see - in Mithila, if you come with us.

verses.devanagari:
तद्धि यज्ञ फलम् तेन मैथिलेन उत्तमम् धनुः |
याचितम् नर शार्दूल सुनाभम् सर्व दैवतैः
verses.iast:
taddhi yajña phalam tena maithilena uttamam dhanuḥ |
yācitam nara śārdūla sunābham sarva daivataiḥ
verses.translation: "Once Devaraata, the grandparent of the present king Janaka of Mithila, conducted a Vedic-ritual and he indeed prayed only for this supreme bow with a best grip-handle as the fruit of that ritual from all of the gods and oh, tigerly man Rama, he got the same from them.
notes: For this kūrma purāṇa, padma puraṇna puts it as: prītaḥ ca bhagavān īsaḥ trisūlī nīla lohitaḥ | pradadau satru nāsārtham janakāya adbhutam dhanuḥ || kūrma purāṇa | | cāpam śambhoḥ dayāt dattam - padma purāṇa 'Satisfying with the ritual of Devaraata of Janaka, the Trident holder and holder of venom in throat, namely god Shiva, gave the marvellous bow to eliminate enemies.'

glosses.meaning: best, at navel [at central grip, handle]
by him, by king of Mithila - namely Devarata

verses.devanagari:
आयागभूतम् नृपतेः तस्य वेश्मनि राघव |
अर्चितम् विविधैः गन्धैः धूपैः च अगुरु गंध्भिः
verses.iast:
āyāgabhūtam nṛpateḥ tasya veśmani rāghava |
arcitam vividhaiḥ gandhaiḥ dhūpaiḥ ca aguru gandhbhiḥ
verses.translation: "That bow has got a regular worship and especially during the periods of dhanur utsava-s, festivals of bows-and- arrows. Hence it is kept in the palace of King of Mithila, and oh, Raghava it is worshipped with a variety of sandalwood pastes, scents of aloe substance, and with incenses."

glosses.meaning: that which is primarily worshipped in dhanur utsava-s, bow-and-arrow worship ceremony
with a variety of, sandalwood pastes
with the substance of true aloe [aloe vera,] its scents

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा मुनिवरः प्रस्थानम् अकरोत् तदा |
स ऋषि संघः स काकुत्स्थ आमंत्र्य वन देवताः
verses.iast:
evam uk{}tvā munivaraḥ prasthānam akarot tadā |
sa ṛṣi saṅghaḥ sa kākutstha āmantrya vana devatāḥ
verses.translation: Saying so that best saint Vishvamitra started to travel on along with the assemblages of sages, and even along with Rama and Lakshmana, whose tacit consent to follow the sage is obtained by now, and on bidding farewell to the deities of woodlands of that Accomplished Hermitage, where his ritual is accomplished with the help of Rama and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: with, Rama, Lakshmana - who by now may be assumed to have said 'yes' speechlessly
to woodland, deities of, bidding farewell

verses.devanagari:
स्वस्ति वो अस्तु गमिष्यामि सिद्धः सिद्ध आश्रमात् अहम् |
उत्तरे जाह्नवी तीरे हिमवंतम् शिलोच्चयम्
verses.iast:
svasti vo astu gamiṣyāmi siddhaḥ siddha āśramāt aham |
uttare jāhnavī tīre himavantam śiloccayam
verses.translation: "Adieu, georgic deities, everything bodes well to you all, on accomplishment of the ritual I have undertaken here, I wish to go from this Accomplished Hermitage towards the ranges of Himalayan Mountains that are on the northern bank of River Ganga."

glosses.meaning: to you all, safe, let become - everything bodes well to you all
on accomplishment [of my work, of ritual]
I am, from the Accomplished, Hermitage
which is there at - northern, Ganga's, bank

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलः कौशिकः स तपोधनः |
उत्तराम् दिशम् उद्दिश्य प्रस्थातुम् उपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
iti uk{}tvā muniśārdūlaḥ kauśikaḥ sa tapodhanaḥ |
uttarām diśam uddiśya prasthātum upacakrame
verses.translation: Thus saying farewell to woodland-deities that descendent of Kaushika, namely Vishvamitra, the saint whose wealth is his ascesis started to journey on aiming to reach the northern side of River Ganga.

glosses.itrans: saH kaushikaH he that, Kaushika's - descendent - Vishvamitra, tapo dhanaH
glosses.iast: saḥ kauśikaḥ he that, Kauśika's - descendent - Viśvamitra, tapo dhanaḥ
glosses.devanagari: सः कौशिकः हे थत्, Kऔशिक'स् देस्चेन्देन्त् Vइश्वमित्र, तपो धनः

verses.devanagari:
तम् व्रजंतम् मुनिवरम् अन्वगात् अनुसारिणाम् |
शकटी शत मात्रम् तु प्रयाणे ब्रह्म वादिनाम्
verses.iast:
tam vrajantam munivaram anvagāt anusāriṇām |
śakaṭī śata mātram tu prayāṇe brahma vādinām
verses.translation: While that best saint set forth, the team of his close followers who are the advocators of Vedic canons have moved behind him, approximately with a hundred carts loaded with their ritual paraphernalia.

verses.devanagari:
मृग पक्षि गणाः चैव सिद्ध आश्रम निवासिनः |
अनुजग्मुर् महात्मानम् विश्वामित्रम् तपोधनम्
निवर्तयामास ततः स ऋसि सन्घः स पक्षिणः |
verses.iast:
mṛga pakṣi gaṇāḥ caiva siddha āśrama nivāsinaḥ |
anujagmur mahātmānam viśvāmitram tapodhanam
nivartayāmāsa tataḥ sa ṛsi sanghaḥ sa pakśiṇaḥ |
verses.translation: Even the residents of that Hermitage of Accomplishment, namely animals and birds, closely followed that great-souled Vishvamitra, whose wealth is his ascesis, in herds and flocks. But that sage Vishvamitra made those flocks of birds and the herds of animals to return to their places, as they have shown enough courtesy.
notes: This following of animals and birds is to suggest that while any guest proceeding from their place, it is the courtesy of the residents of that place or house, to see him off for a distance, unlike 'showing a person the door.' Here Vishvamitra is the guest at these woodlands.

glosses.meaning: animals, birds, herds / flocks of, also, even
great, souled one, ascetically, wealthy, after Vishvamitra
back, made to turn - caused to return to their places.

verses.devanagari:
ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् लम्बमाने दिवाकरे
वासम् चक्रुर् मुनि गणाः शोणा कूले समाहिताः |
verses.iast:
te gatvā dūram adhvānam lambamāne divākare
vāsam cakrur muni gaṇāḥ śoṇā kūle samāhitāḥ |
verses.translation: Those assemblages of sages on going far on their path made a camp on the bank of River Sona when the sun is dangling towards west.

glosses.meaning: far, on the way, on going
day, maker - sun, while dangling - towards west
River Sona, on the bank of

verses.devanagari:
ते अस्तम् गते दिनकरे स्नात्वा हुत हुताशनाः
विश्वामित्रम् पुरस्कृत्य निषेदुर् अमित ओजसः |
verses.iast:
te astam gate dinakare snātvā huta hutāśanāḥ
viśvāmitram puraskṛtya niṣedur amita ojasaḥ |
verses.translation: When the sun went into dusk those sages with illimitable resplendence took their bath and on kindling the consumer of kindled oblations they completed their evening fire ritual, and then squatted before sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: day, maker - sun, dusk, when entered
that which is kindled, consumer of it - Ritual fire - consuming items oblated in fire

verses.devanagari:
रामो अपि सह सौमित्रिः मुनीम् तान् अभिपूज्य च
अग्रतो निषसाद अथ विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः |
verses.iast:
rāmo api saha saumitriḥ munīm tān abhipūjya ca
agrato niṣasāda atha viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ |
verses.translation: And even Rama along with Lakshmana on worshipping those sages squatted before that intellectual Vishvamitra.

verses.devanagari:
अथ रामो महातेजा विश्वामित्रम् तपोधनम्
पप्रच्छ मुनिशार्दूलम् कौतूहल समन्वितः |
verses.iast:
atha rāmo mahātejā viśvāmitram tapodhanam
papraccha muniśārdūlam kautūhala samanvitaḥ |
verses.translation: With growing inquisitiveness that resplendent Rama has asked the tigerly sage Vishvamitra whose wealth is his ascesis.

verses.devanagari:
भगवन् कः नु अयम् देशः समृद्ध वन शोभितः
श्रोतुम् इच्छामि भद्रम् ते वक्तुम् अर्हसि तत्त्वतः |
verses.iast:
bhagavan kaḥ nu ayam deśaḥ samṛddha vana śobhitaḥ
śrotum icchāmi bhadram te vak{}tum arhasi tattvataḥ |
verses.translation: "Oh, godly sage, this place is glistening with well-developed woodlands, really what is this place? You be blest! It will be apt of you tell about it, in essence." Thus Rama asked Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: to you, let there be safety - you be blest
in essence, to talk - to tell, apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
चोदितो राम वाक्येन कथयामास सुव्रतः |
तस्य देशस्य निखिलम् ऋषि मध्ये महातपाः
verses.iast:
codito rāma vākyena kathayāmāsa suvrataḥ |
tasya deśasya nikhilam ṛṣi madhye mahātapāḥ
verses.translation: Sage Vishvamitra whose vows are unselfish and whose ascesis is exalted is motivated with the words of Rama and staying amidst the sages he started to tell all about that place. [1-31-24b, c]
